title: The Fallen
summary: Rebel angels loosed from the Abyss into mortal bodies.

claims.text: The fallen are the angels who rose against Heaven; demon is both a word for one lost to hate and madness, and a loose name for all of them.
The Elohim are the Creator's servants, the beings people call angels; Celestials covers angels and demons alike.
Demons turn up all over the world but gather most in the great cities, where human faith is thickest.

title: The Fall and the Age of Wrath
summary: Lucifer's rebellion and the war that followed.

claims.text: The Fall was Lucifer and a third of the Elohim waking humanity to awareness, which began the Age of Wrath.
The Age of Wrath was the thousand-year war between Heaven and the fallen.
A faction of the fallen still seeks Lucifer, who vanished, and wants the war against Heaven resumed.

title: The Abyss
summary: The prison the Creator made for the fallen.

claims.text: The Abyss, also called the Pit, is the prison built by the Creator to hold the rebel angels.
Its gates are now broken, and the fallen walk free once more.
Most warlords, House elders and faction leaders are still trapped there, so each freed demon chooses whom to follow.

title: The Sebettu
summary: The seven rebel Houses.

claims.text: Sebettu means the Seven: the rebel Houses of the fallen.
A House is an angelic hierarchy given one task in making and watching over the cosmos.
Before the Fall each House had an autarch leading a council of lieutenants, with no rise or fall in rank.
The rebels rebuilt their House order soon after breaking away, and Lucifer never tried to dissolve it.
A demon's starting Torment depends on the House.

title: Namaru (Devils)
summary: Rebel angels of the dawn.

claims.text: Namaru is the proper name of the House of the dawn; Devils is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 4.
House lores: the Celestials, Flame and Radiance.

title: Asharu (Scourges)
summary: Rebel angels of the winds.

claims.text: Asharu is the proper name of the House of the wind; Scourges is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 3.
House lores: the Winds, Awakening and the Firmament.

title: Annunaki (Malefactors)
summary: Rebel angels of the earth.

claims.text: Annunaki is the proper name of the House of the earth; Malefactors is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 3.
House lores: the Earth, the Forge and Paths.

title: Lammasu (Defilers)
summary: Rebel angels of the sea.

claims.text: Lammasu is the proper name of the House of the sea; Defilers is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 3.
House lores: Longing, Storms and Transfiguration.
Before the Fall they were the Nereids, angels of the first oceans, meant to stir mortals toward art, mystery and discovery.
Defilers most often join the Faustians or the Raveners.

title: Neberu (Fiends)
summary: Rebel angels of the heavens.

claims.text: Neberu is the proper name of the House of the heavens; Fiends is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 3.
House lores: Light, Patterns and Portals.

title: Rabisu (Devourers)
summary: Rebel angels of the wild.

claims.text: Rabisu is the proper name of the House of the wild; Devourers is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 4.
House lores: the Beast, the Flesh and the Wild.

title: Halaku (Slayers)
summary: Rebel angels of the dead.

claims.text: Halaku is the proper name of the House of the dead; Slayers is the common one.
Starting Torment for this House is 4.
House lores: Death, the Realms and the Spirit.

title: The Five Factions
summary: The philosophies that split the fallen.

claims.text: Cryptics want the truth behind Lucifer's vanishing and the other unanswered questions of the Fall.
Faustians would enslave humankind and turn it into a weapon against Heaven.
Luciferans seek Lucifer and a return to the war.
Raveners want the universe destroyed.
Reconcilers would make Earth the paradise it was before the Age of Wrath.
Five factions divide the seven Houses.

title: The Earthbound
summary: Ancient demons anchored in the world.

claims.text: The Earthbound were called out of the Abyss in ancient times and found a way to fix themselves in the physical world.
They now try to enslave or destroy the fallen.

title: Faith (Demon)
summary: The trait that powers a demon.

claims.text: Faith fuels evocations, heals damage and lets a demon take on supernatural forms.
New characters begin with Faith 3; freebie points and experience raise it. Faith costs 6 freebie points a dot.
With no Faith left, a demon can still use powers only by ravaging the mind and soul of thralls.
The broad belief of ancient times has dwindled, leaving freed demons to fight over what remains.

title: Torment
summary: The scar of betrayal and the Abyss on a demon's soul.

claims.text: Torment is the opposite of Faith: the damage done by rebellion, war and ages in the Abyss.
A hierarchy of sins runs from permanent Torment 10, where nothing is a sin, down through casual cruelty, planned harm and sins of passion.
A good deed can be rolled against Torment using Conscience, Conviction or Courage as fits; if Virtue wins, one temporary Torment is lost, and Willpower cannot be spent on the roll.
Ten experience points lower permanent Torment by one.
High-Torment demons favour pacts that corrupt; low-Torment demons lean toward pacts of real gratitude, such as healing the sick.

title: Virtues (Demon)
summary: Conscience, Conviction and Courage.

claims.text: Conscience measures the sense of right and wrong, Conviction the strength of belief, Courage the will to act on it.
Each Virtue starts at one dot, with three more to share among them.
Starting Willpower is the total of the two highest Virtues.

title: Apocalyptic Form
summary: A demon's true shape, shown in the flesh.

claims.text: The apocalyptic form, or visage, is the bodily echo of a demon's Celestial nature.
Each form has four high-Torment powers: one may be added at permanent Torment 7, another at 8, and so on.
When permanent Torment drops, high-Torment powers go one per point, newest first; low-Torment abilities stay.
In danger a demon may call up a high-Torment power for one scene, at the cost of temporary Torment.

title: Revelation
summary: What happens when a demon's nature shows itself to mortals.

claims.text: Revelation is always powerful for a mortal who sees it.
It also signals the demon's presence to anyone able to feel Creation being tampered with, which makes hiding harder.

title: Lore
summary: The commands of Creation that make up a demon's powers.

claims.text: Lore is the source of Celestial power: the gathered commands for working the fabric of reality.
There are twenty-three lores; each House has three, and Humanity and the Fundament are open to all.
A lore dot costs 7 freebie points.

title: Pacts and Thralls
summary: How demons draw Faith from mortals.

claims.text: A thrall is a mortal bound to a demon by a pact of faith.
A pact is a spoken bargain freely made: a service in return for a channel to the mortal's spiritual strength, which works at any distance.
It must be voluntary, though it can be struck under duress; doubt before the demon delivers breaks it.
Reaping faith from fear or awe gives a quick return that fades, and the same person grows jaded if reaped too often; a pact gives a steady supply.
Pacts is also a Background: mortal sources of Faith.

title: Legacy
summary: How much a demon remembers of angelic life.

claims.text: Legacy is the Background for how much of the divine existence before the host the demon recalls.
Eminence is standing among other demons; Paragon is special strength in one part of the House's domain.
